source_text.body:
Draft batch prospecting emails and prep sales work
Account executives have Claude draft batch prospecting emails in Gmail for approval, and run a computer agent connected to HubSpot, email and call transcripts to prep their work.
·
Jul 17, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
In the thread, AEs describe two concrete setups. One has Claude integrated with CRM and Gmail to do territory research, find contacts, upload them into the CRM, generate a morning brief, and draft emails in Gmail for the rep to approve and send; they also mention iterating prompts when Claude misses context in email and call data. Another says their internal AI agent is connected to systems like HubSpot-style CRM, email, Slack, usage and billing data, docs, pricing tools, and call or transcript sources, then scans them on a schedule to prioritize work, prep meetings, draft updates, and handle notes while the seller reviews before sending.
How it went
The reported result was mainly time saved and better coverage: one user said it felt like having a full-time BDR and admin assistant, and another said it saved a lot of time and improved the quality of weekly field-insight writeups. Limits mentioned were that full decks were still poor and the briefing agent still missed items or key thread details.
Worth knowing
The main catch was access: people said this only becomes useful when the company allows Claude or similar tools to connect to CRM, Gmail, Slack, and other internal systems.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Using my Gmail and the list of accounts in [spreadsheet or CRM view], draft personalized prospecting emails for [number] contacts, each referencing something specific like [recent call, news, or role]. Save them as Gmail drafts, not sent. Pause and show me the full set for approval before anything is sent, and give me a short prep note for each account.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/techsales/comments/1ufkvbw/how_are_aes_using_ai_in_their_day_to_day_role
